metadata.case_name: WONG SUN CHEONG, SUING BY HIS NEXT FRIEND LEE YIN SHEUNG v. CHOI CHI KONG AND ANOTHER

plaintiff.occupation_before: delivery man at Kai Ming Food Shop

source: P sustained severe head injuries as is borne out by the agreed medical evidence.

injuries.description: Fractures on the left side of his skull
source: Radiological investigations showed fractures on the left side of his skull, subarachnoid bleeding, subdural bleeding as well as contusion of the brain substance.
injuries.icd_description: Fracture of skull or facial bones, part unspecified

In August 2012, while having lunch at home, he developed status epilepticus with refractory generalized epileptic seizures.
He was then started on the antiepileptic drug phenytoin which he continues to take. He has been seizure‑free since that one occasion.
injuries.icd_description: Epilepsy due to injuries to the head

manifestations.description: prolonged post‑traumatic amnesia (estimated as over one month)
dysphasia (problem with language); impaired ability to express himself; naming difficulty; often using the wrong words; slowed comprehension
cognitive dysfunction; scored 18/30 on mini mental state examination (mild to moderate dementia)
impaired balance; truncal ataxia; could not walk heel to toe; able to stand with feet together and eyes closed
right leg mild spasticity with heightened reflexes
epileptic seizures (status epilepticus in August 2012, then seizure‑free since)
not employable in any capacity; permanent loss of earning capacity 100%

treatments_received: Emergency operation to evacuate blood clots and to insert a ventricular drain
Second emergency operation to evacuate more blood clots
Cranioplasty to repair the skull defect with a metallic prosthesis (May 2012)
Intubation and time in intensive care unit
Transfer to an old peoples home

losses.description: Severe head injury with skull fractures and intracranial bleeding
Cognitive dysfunction; mild to moderate dementia (MMSE 18/30) and slowed comprehension
Dysphasia; naming difficulty; impaired ability to express himself
Not fully independent inside the home; not capable of managing his own legal and financial affairs; needs care and attention for the rest of his life
Not employable in any capacity; permanent loss of earning capacity 100%
